name: slow_tick_continuous_watch
description: A 30 s flick watched continuously, but the client's one-second sampler ran late once: three seconds of wall clock and three seconds of playhead passed between two samples. That is watching, not a seek. A correct tracker credits the 3000 ms and reports no seek; the resulting stream is a plain watch whose first heartbeat is a second late.
viewer: 0-6 s: plays; the sample due at 3 s arrives at 6 s (the tab was busy), with the playhead at 6 s
6-30 s: plays to the end on a regular tick
notes: Divergence 3 (M-12, web side closed as M-27): the seek ceiling is sized from the elapsed time actually measured between the two samples, max(elapsed, SAMPLE_INTERVAL_MS) x 2 x speed, never from the nominal interval alone. The web tracker does this: MomentumVideo passes the measured elapsed to sample() and watchTracker.ts sizes the ceiling from it, so this stream is what it emits; the unit test in packages/player/src/watchTracker.test.ts (a slow tick is not a seek) pins it. Android still sizes the ceiling from the constant and has no measured elapsed at all, so against this fixture it reports watched_ms_total 3000 short and seek_count_increment 1 — the remaining target for the next Android session.
